_comment: Tune this file, not the code. Level descriptions are sent to Jev verbatim as criteria, so rewording them changes the judgments. Weights, thresholds, and estimate bands are applied in code after the model answers, so changing them re-derives priority and estimates WITHOUT a new API call (see 'Retuning is free' in SKILL.md).

instructions.question: How badly is the person filing this blocked from doing what they set out to do?
instructions.focus: Judge the impact described, not how upset the reporter sounds. A calmly worded outage is still an outage; an angry report about a typo is still a typo.

criteria.what: Cosmetic or textual. Everything works; something looks wrong or reads wrong.
A feature is degraded or awkward, but the person can still complete the task.
examples: confusing error copy that still lets you recover

criteria.what: A feature is broken with no workaround. The person cannot complete this task at all, but the rest of the product works.
Data loss, data corruption, a security exposure, or an outage of the whole product.
examples: one account can read another's data

instructions.question: How many of the product's users run into this?
instructions.focus: Judge the affected population, not the number of reports. A single observed occurrence is not evidence of narrow reach unless the report explains why other users are unaffected. If the evidence is one case but nothing bounds it to that case, the population is unknown and probably broad.

criteria.what: Confined to one account or configuration, and the report gives a specific reason it would not affect anyone else.
examples: a setting only this customer uses

criteria.what: A narrow but identifiable slice defined by something the report names: one platform, one integration, one plan tier, one locale.
Anyone who uses a common feature, or an unknown population that the evidence does not bound — few observed occurrences but no stated reason others are safe.
examples: one crash report in a shared code path
a single 503 with no explanation of why it is isolated

criteria.what: Effectively everyone, or anyone attempting a core flow such as signing in, loading the app, or saving work.

instructions.question: Is there a deadline or ongoing damage that makes waiting costly?
instructions.focus: Look for an external date, a contractual or compliance obligation, or harm that accumulates while the issue is open. Absence of urgent wording is not itself evidence of low urgency.

criteria.what: No deadline. Waiting a release or two costs nothing in particular.
A real but soft date: a launch, a customer demo, a sprint boundary that this is meant to land before.
Damage accrues every day it stays open, or a hard external deadline has passed or is imminent.

weights._comment: Must sum to 1.0. These encode what your team means by 'important'. Raise reach if you optimize for breadth; raise severity if you optimize for depth of pain.

priority_thresholds._comment: Composite urgency (0..1) mapped to Linear's priority enum. Linear's numbering is inverted from intuition: 1=Urgent is the MOST urgent, 4=Low the least. Bands are checked top down.

confidence._comment: Confidence measures how concentrated the model's probability distribution is, NOT whether it is right. Tiering uses a weight-aware average of the priority dimensions plus work_kind, because a min() across everything lets one structurally-uncertain dimension drag every issue into the bottom tier. Dimensions below uncertain_below are surfaced by name instead.

effort._comment: Sizing dimensions, scored independently and combined in code exactly as the priority dimensions are. Asking 'how many points is this?' directly returns a number you cannot argue with; three dimensions return evidence you can re-band when the team's velocity changes. Levels must describe situations a reader could tell apart without seeing their neighbours — see 'When the judgments look wrong' in SKILL.md.

instructions.question: How much of the product has to change to close this?
instructions.focus: Judge the extent of the change, not how hard it is to work out. A sweeping but mechanical rename is wide; a one-line fix that takes a week to find is narrow. Difficulty is asked about separately.

criteria.what: One contained edit in a single place, with no decisions attached to it.
One component or one flow, end to end. Several edits, all in the same area, all identifiable up front.
examples: add a field to an existing form and persist it

criteria.what: Several areas have to change together, or something new has to be built and wired into what already exists.
examples: add CSV export: new endpoint, new UI, new permission check
thread a new setting through client and server

criteria.what: Structural. A schema, protocol, or public interface changes, or existing data has to be migrated, so the full set of edits cannot be listed before starting.
examples: backfill and re-key an existing table

instructions.question: How much has to be figured out before someone could start writing the fix?
instructions.focus: Judge what is not yet known, separately from how much code changes. An unreproduced crash is full of unknowns even if the fix turns out to be one line.

criteria.what: Nothing to work out. The change itself is stated or obvious from the report, and someone could start immediately.
The approach is clear; the details are not. Which call, which place, which edge cases — all answerable while working, without a separate investigation.
The cause or the design has to be investigated first, and that investigation is bounded: there is a clear place to start looking and it is likely to find an answer.
examples: reproducible crash with no obvious cause
a design that has to be chosen before building

criteria.what: It is not yet known whether this can be solved as framed. The work could turn out to be far larger than it looks, or turn out not to be the real problem at all.
examples: a fix that may require a dependency to change first

instructions.question: How much does finishing this depend on people or systems outside the person doing the work?
instructions.focus: Judge dependency, not team size. Work that needs a design, another team's deploy, or a third party's change is coordinated even when the code is trivial.

criteria.what: One person can carry this from start to done on their own, with ordinary review.
Something is needed from someone else along the way — a design, a decision, a review from another team — but the work can start without it.
examples: needs copy from design before it ships
needs a product decision on the edge case

criteria.what: Cannot be finished without a party outside this team, a sequenced deploy or migration, or a dependency that does not exist yet.
examples: requires a coordinated client and server release
needs a data migration run in production

estimation._comment: Everything here is policy applied AFTER the model answers, so 'our 5s are too big' is a band change and a retune.mjs run, not a re-judgment. Linear's scales are non-linear, so mapping effort to a value is a band lookup, never arithmetic: 8 on the Fibonacci scale is not twice the effort of 4.

weights._comment: Must sum to 1.0. Scope dominates because it is the part a reviewer can check. Raise unknowns if your team's estimates keep getting blown out by investigation rather than by volume.

bands._comment: Effort (0..1) to a POSITION on the team's scale, not to a value — index 0 is the smallest value the team uses, whatever it happens to be. Upper bound of each band, checked top down. Deliberately stops at index 4: the extended values (Fibonacci 13/21, exponential 32/64) exist for work that should be split instead, and this skill proposes the split rather than the number.

estimation._min_estimable_note: Below this the estimate is withheld rather than guessed. A fabricated number is worse than an empty field, because Linear feeds estimates into cycle capacity and project graphs where nobody can see it was a shrug.
estimation._min_actionable_note: If nobody can tell what 'done' means, the size of getting there is not a real quantity either.

split._comment: Linear's own guidance: a large estimate usually means uncertainty rather than volume, and the right move is to break the issue up. When the work lands in the top band AND the unknowns are high, propose a split instead of a number.

estimation._propose_zero_note: An explicit 0 asserts the work costs nothing, which is a human's call and not something to infer from a description. Left unestimated instead, even on teams that allow zero.
estimation._reestimate_existing_note: By default only unestimated issues get a proposal. A number already in the field usually came from a person who knew more than the issue text does; overwriting it silently is the expensive mistake. Ask for a re-estimate explicitly to override.

scales._comment: From Linear's estimate docs. T-shirt sizes are stored as the Fibonacci numbers and only displayed as letters. Zero is a separate 'allow zero estimates' setting and is never part of the ordered scale.

pr_metrics._comment: Sizing completed work from the PRs that delivered it (scripts/pr-metrics.mjs, needs the gh CLI). Measured once against a real milestone: judged estimates correlated with churn at only 0.37 and ran systematically small, so a merged PR is better evidence than a description wherever one exists. See “What the estimates are worth” in SKILL.md.
pr_metrics._churn_bands_note: Ascending upper bounds on churn (additions + deletions) mapping to positions on the team’s scale: <50 index 0, <200 index 1, <600 index 2, <2000 index 3, else index 4. Log-ish on purpose — churn spanned 9 to 6,706 in one milestone, and linear cuts would collapse almost everything into one bucket.
pr_metrics._iteration_bump_at_note: Commits + human reviews + human comments at or above this move the estimate one position up, never down. Heavy iteration means the change was argued over, which is effort the diff size does not show.
pr_metrics._bot_authors_note: Substring match on the PR review/comment author login. Bot chatter is not review effort, and counting it would reward noisy automation. Linear’s own linkback comment appears on every linked PR.
pr_metrics._not_used_note: Wall-clock time to merge is reported per PR but never scored on. It measures calendar latency, not effort: on the calibration run a 4,030-line PR merged in 0.0 hours while a 13-line one took 49.
pr_metrics._count_abandoned_churn_note: true (this config): churn counts every linked PR, so effort spent on attempts that never merged is part of the size. false: churn counts only what shipped, and abandoned work is reported as abandoned_churn but not sized. Either way the rework also counts as iteration. Pick the one that matches what the team means by velocity — change delivered, or effort spent.

labels._comment: Real workspaces carry far more labels than are worth judging per issue. Candidates are shortlisted in code before the model sees them; these settings control that shortlist. Tuned against the Tlon team's 99 labels.
labels._exclude_groups_note: Release/version tags are bookkeeping applied at ship time, not a semantic judgment about the issue.
labels._always_consider_note: Groups listed here are judged even when no child is applied yet, which is how an untriaged Reliability issue gets its phase.
labels._kind_label_map_note: These labels are driven by the work_kind Choice instead of separate Nouls, so the two cannot disagree.
labels._group_gates_note: Ask the group question speculatively, then keep the answer only when the gating label also scored high. A forced Choice always picks something, so the gate — not the model — decides whether the group applies at all.
